data.body:
Plan review BLOCKED on one finding. Verified against the code; it is right, and it caught a repeat of a mistake that has already cost two close refusals in this epic.

The finding: the plan adds a derived key to derive_policy_sets but never enumerates the census test that pins the exact key set. Confirmed at tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py:81 — test_derive_covers_exactly_the_census_set_names asserts set(derived) == set(_CENSUS_SETS) against the hardcoded 17-name tuple at :28. Adding a key fails that assertion until the tuple names it.

Two things follow. The test must change, so it belongs in file_impact — and it was NOT declared. That is exactly what made the close gate refuse ce8f and e755 earlier today: work touching files the reviewed plan never named. Catching it at review time rather than at close time saves a whole widen-and-re-review cycle.

Reading the test also surfaced a detail the plan had not accounted for: _all_current_spellings at :74 deliberately SKIPS the overlay sets (_CONFIRM_SCOPE, _LEGACY_OUTPUT, _NO_AUTO_MOUNT) because their members already appear in a base set. The warn set is the same shape — an overlay, not a partition — so it must join that skip list or the spelling census will double-count its members.

Plan now names the census test and the overlay skip list, adds AC5 pinning both, and file_impact declares tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py. file_impact was widened BEFORE the re-review, so the attestation basis is correct. Re-review started.
